name: Jingpho (Kachin, Jinghpaw)

ancestors.notes: Sino-Tibetan (Trans-Himalayan). Jingpho belongs to the Jingpho-Sal (Jingpho-Konyak-Bodo / Sal) branch, a SISTER of Kuki-Chin proper -- not a Kuki-Chin daughter (Burling 1983; van Driem 2001; Glottolog 'jing1260' is coordinate with, not under, 'kuki1246') -- so it is not parented to mni-x-proto-kuki-chin.

notes: Jingpho (Jinghpaw, Kachin), spoken mainly in Kachin State, Myanmar, and Yunnan, China (as Jingpo). Jingpho-Sal branch of Sino-Tibetan (Burling 1983). Written with a Latin-based alphabet (23 letters) devised by Baptist missionary Ola Hanson from 1890; an unofficial Mon-Burmese-derived system also exists but Latin is the primary/official orthography (Wikipedia; Kurabe 2016). Aspirated stops/affricates are spelled with a preposed ⟨h⟩ digraph (⟨hp ht hk hts hc⟩) rather than a postposed one as in most neighbouring Kuki-Chin orthographies -- this is the orthography's own device for the aspirate series and each digraph earns its key on the same grounds as postposed-h digraphs elsewhere (AGENTS.md test 2). ⟨ny⟩ spells the palatal nasal /ɲ/; ⟨ng⟩ the velar nasal /ŋ/; ⟨j⟩ spells the voiced alveolar affricate /dz/ and ⟨c/hc⟩ the palatal affricate series, per Kurabe (2016). Jingpho has four tones in open syllables and two in closed syllables (Kurabe 2016; Wikipedia); tone diacritics (á a à â) are optional/inconsistently used in ordinary writing, so tone is left unmarked in this grapheme map pending a citable, consistently-applied tone orthography. Diphthong digraphs (ai au oi ui) each spell one syllable nucleus (AGENTS.md test 2). ⟨ts⟩ spells the single alveolar affricate phoneme /ts/, listed in AGENTS.md itself as a canonical passing multigraph, not a stop+fricative cluster. Letter values corrected against Wikipedia's Jinghpaw alphabet table: the palatal affricate is spelled ⟨chy⟩ [tɕ] (no bare ⟨c⟩ letter exists, and no ⟨hc⟩ digraph is attested — an earlier draft's ⟨c⟩/⟨hc⟩ keys were removed as unsupported); ⟨j⟩ is [dʑ]; ⟨hts⟩ [tsʰ]; the palatalized stop series is written ⟨ky gy hky hpy⟩; ⟨aw⟩ spells [ɔ].
